demonstrates: Manifest-declared property typing, which is the gap ruling 4 assigned to A2. A record carrying a prefixed property the manifest never declared is rejected; so is a prefixed property belonging to another Field, an unprefixed name outside the shared registry, a declared property emitted with the wrong scalar type, and a core-owned property a Field must never supply.
notes: Before A2 there was no registry entry for a prefixed property, so its type was inferred from canonical spelling. The declaring manifest replaces that inference for declared properties. Each case here is its own conformance run.

note: 'local_inode_number' carries the Field's own registered prefix but is absent from the manifest's declared_properties.

detail: The prefix is this Field's, but the declaring manifest does not list the property, so core has no approved type or list semantics for it and rejects it rather than inferring one. Declaring it is a manifest change reviewed with the Field's release.

Local reference material describing the rollout checklist.

note: A registered prefix belonging to a different Field.

detail: A Note's prefixed properties must belong to its own Field's registered stem. A 'teams_' property from the local connector is a connector-boundary violation regardless of whether the Teams Field declares it.

# Rollout reference

Local reference material describing the rollout checklist.

note: An unprefixed name that is not in the closed shared registry.

detail: Shared unprefixed properties are closed by the A1 registry and a Field cannot invent one. The Field's options are an approved shared property or its own declared prefixed property.

note: Two declared properties emitted with the wrong shape: 'local_document_flag' is declared text but arrives as a JSON boolean, and 'local_tags' is declared a list but arrives as a scalar.

detail: The manifest declares the type and cardinality, so a disagreement is a Field defect rather than a new type. This is what stops a property's type from drifting inside one notebook.

note: A Field trying to assign a record ID and a content hash. Structurally impossible: the property-name grammar of the record schema excludes every core-owned and hoisted name, so this frame does not validate at all.

detail: Core owns record IDs, producer provenance, capture time, hashes, and every rebuildable projection. A Field that supplies them is rejected at the schema, not merely overruled later.
